text: When the people saw that Moses was slow to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, Get up and make us gods who will go ahead of us, because we don't know what has happened to this Moses who brought us out of Egypt.
Aaron told them, Take off the gold earrings that your wives, sons, and daughters are wearing, and bring them to me.
So all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from them, shaped it with a tool, and formed it into an image of a calf. Then they said, Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up out of Egypt!
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, Tomorrow will be a festival to the LORD.
Early the next day they got up, offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings, and the people sat down to eat and drink, then got up to celebrate wildly.
The LORD said to Moses, Go down at once, because your people, the ones you brought out of Egypt, have ruined themselves.
They have already turned away from what I commanded them — they made themselves a metal calf, worshiped it, sacrificed to it, and said, These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.
The LORD told Moses, I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stubborn people.
Now leave me alone, so my anger can burn against them and destroy them — then I will make you into a great nation instead.
But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God: LORD, why should your anger burn against your own people, the ones you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians be able to say, He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the earth? Turn from your fierce anger; relent, and don't bring this disaster on your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by your own self that you would multiply their descendants like the stars in the sky, and give this whole land you promised to their descendants forever.
So the LORD relented and did not bring on his people the disaster he had said he would.
Moses turned and went down the mountain, carrying the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, written on both sides, front and back.
The tablets were God's own work, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, There is the sound of war in the camp.
But Moses said, It's not the sound of victory or the sound of defeat — it's the sound of singing that I hear.
As Moses got closer to the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned; he threw the tablets down and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it, ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses asked Aaron, What did these people do to you, that you led them into such a great sin?
Aaron answered, Don't be angry, my lord — you know how prone these people are to evil.
They told me, Make us gods to go ahead of us, because we don't know what happened to this Moses who brought us out of Egypt.
So I told them, Whoever has gold, take it off — and they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!
Moses saw that the people were running wild, since Aaron had let them get out of control, an embarrassment in front of their enemies.
So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and called out, Whoever is on the LORD's side, come to me! And all the Levites gathered around him.

He told them, This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Each of you strap on your sword, go back and forth through the camp from one gate to the other, and kill your brother, your friend, and your neighbor.
The Levites did as Moses commanded, and about three thousand people died that day.
Moses said, Today you have been dedicated to the LORD, each of you at the cost of his son or his brother, so that he may bless you this day.
The next day Moses told the people, You have committed a terrible sin. But now I will go up to the LORD — maybe I can make things right for your sin.
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, This people has committed a terrible sin, making themselves a god out of gold.
But now, please forgive their sin — and if not, please blot me out of the book you have written.
The LORD replied to Moses, Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot that person out of my book.
Now go, lead the people to where I told you, and my angel will go ahead of you — but on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.
So the LORD struck the people with a plague, because of what they did with the calf that Aaron made.
